# AMD Instinct validation campaign for vLLM serving parity

## Description

Run a validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct accelerator nodes to
establish first-hand functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving
of the platform's supported model set on ROCm. The campaign produces the
go/no-go recommendation and the cleared-model list that scopes productization
of a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime. This resolves the strategy's central
unknown: upstream vLLM publishes ROCm support, but the platform has no
first-hand parity data for its supported models.

## Scope

- Secure access to dedicated AMD Instinct nodes (procurement or partner-lab
  access — currently unresolved; this is a precondition for campaign start).
- Define the functional and performance parity criteria and thresholds for
  the go/no-go decision (the strategy does not state quantitative thresholds).
- For each model in the supported model set, run vLLM serving on ROCm using
  upstream ROCm runtime images and record:
  - functional correctness of serving (successful loads, inference outputs);
  - performance measurements relative to the comparable CUDA baseline.
- Produce a go/no-go report per model with a recommended productization scope
  (the cleared-model list) and any remediation findings (driver versions,
  image versions, known ROCm issues encountered).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given access to physical AMD Instinct nodes, when the supported model set
  is served with vLLM on ROCm, then functional and performance parity data
  exists for every model in the set, measured by a per-model test record with
  defined pass/fail criteria against the agreed thresholds.
- Given the collected parity data, when the campaign concludes, then a
  go/no-go recommendation with a cleared-model list is published, measured by
  a report accepted by the strategy stakeholders.
- Given the campaign findings, when ROCm-specific constraints are found
  (driver prerequisites, image versions, model-specific failures), then they
  are documented for the productization and documentation work that follows.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware
  establishing functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the
  supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

Productize a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models cleared by
the AMD Instinct validation campaign, so that RHOAI can serve those models on
AMD accelerators. Today only CUDA (NVIDIA) runtime builds are productized;
upstream vLLM publishes ROCm builds that are not shipped or supported. This
epic turns the validated subset into a productized runtime.

## Scope

- Build and release a vLLM ROCm serving runtime image from the existing
  midstream vLLM repos, for the model set cleared by the validation campaign.
- Pin the image to an upstream ROCm runtime release aligned with the platform
  release train (upstream cadence is AMD/community-controlled; tracking and
  digest pinning is part of this scope).
- Provide the ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime templates that expose the
  ROCm runtime for AMD Instinct nodes, requesting amd.com/gpu resources.
- Validate that KServe InferenceServices using the ROCm serving runtime
  schedule and serve correctly on AMD Instinct nodes (KServe itself requires
  no code changes — this is the passive-component validation).
- Ensure the build pipeline for the ROCm image variant is green through the
  onboarded Konflux setup (the pipeline onboarding runs in parallel; its
  first green execution gates release, not development).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the cleared-model list from the validation campaign, when the ROCm
  serving runtime is productized, then every cleared model serves
  successfully on AMD Instinct nodes via KServe InferenceServices, measured
  by end-to-end serving tests per cleared model.
- Given the ROCm runtime image, when it is released, then the image digest is
  pinned to an upstream ROCm release compatible with the platform release
  train, measured by the release manifest.
- Given an InferenceService selecting the ROCm serving runtime, when deployed
  to a node pool with AMD Instinct accelerators, then pods schedule with
  amd.com/gpu resources and become Ready, measured by InferenceService status
  conditions.
- Given the Konflux build pipeline for the ROCm image variant, when a change
  lands, then the pipeline builds the image green, measured by a passing
  Konflux build for the runtime image.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the
  models the validation campaign clears.

## Risks

- Upstream ROCm image release cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream
  communities and may not align with platform release trains.
- Full no-go from the validation campaign removes this epic; a partial
  cleared-model list rewrites its scope.

# Konflux build pipeline for the vLLM ROCm serving image

## Description

Onboard the build pipeline for the new vLLM ROCm serving runtime image
variant into Konflux. The vLLM midstream repos are already Konflux-onboarded
for existing (CUDA) builds; this epic adds the build configuration for the
ROCm image variant so it can be built and released through the standard
platform pipeline. This is a new container image in an existing repo, so no
repo onboarding is needed — once the validation campaign concludes with a go
decision, pipeline onboarding starts and runs in parallel with the runtime
image implementation work (there is no serial repo-onboarding chain; the only
upstream gate is the campaign itself).

## Scope

- Add Konflux build configuration (image variant, build recipe) for the vLLM
  ROCm serving runtime image in the existing onboarded repos.
- Wire the new image variant into the existing release pipeline so it is
  built and published per platform version alongside the CUDA builds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the Konflux configuration for the ROCm image variant, when a build
  is triggered, then the image builds green through Konflux, measured by a
  passing pipeline run producing the ROCm runtime image.
- Given the release pipeline, when a platform version is cut, then the ROCm
  image variant is built and published through the same mechanism as the
  existing runtime builds, measured by the released image artifact.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the
  models the validation campaign clears (build-pipeline enablement).

# PyTorch ROCm training support for Training Operator jobs

## Description

Enable PyTorch training on AMD Instinct accelerators (ROCm) for single- and
multi-GPU jobs run through the Training Operator's PyTorchJob resource.
Upstream PyTorch publishes ROCm support; this epic brings that support to the
platform's training path so data scientists can train on AMD GPUs with the
same job APIs used for NVIDIA GPUs today.

## Scope

- Provide PyTorch ROCm worker images (or approved image references) usable by
  PyTorchJob pods on AMD Instinct nodes, pinned to upstream ROCm releases.
- Ensure PyTorchJob specs can request amd.com/gpu resources for both
  single-GPU and multi-GPU (distributed) job topologies.
- Validate functional training on physical AMD Instinct hardware (hardware
  access is a shared precondition with the serving validation campaign).
- Validate end-to-end admission and execution of multi-GPU PyTorchJobs
  through Kueue with amd.com/gpu quota (the quota configuration itself is
  tracked separately by the Distributed Workloads component; this epic
  verifies jobs flow through it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a PyTorchJob requesting amd.com/gpu resources, when submitted to a
  cluster with AMD Instinct nodes, then the job runs training to completion
  on ROCm, measured by successful job completion status for single-GPU and
  multi-GPU topologies.
- Given a multi-GPU PyTorchJob on ROCm, when submitted through a Kueue-backed
  queue with amd.com/gpu quota configured, then the job is admitted and all
  pods run, measured by Kueue admission state and job completion.
- Given the PyTorch ROCm worker images, when used per documentation, then the
  pinned image references are recorded for release, measured by the release
  manifest.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling.

## Risks

- Requires physical AMD Instinct hardware for validation; access is
  unresolved at strategy level (procurement or partner lab).
- Upstream PyTorch/ROCm image cadence is controlled by AMD and upstream
  communities.

# Kueue quota handling for amd.com/gpu resources

## Description

Extend the Distributed Workloads queueing layer so that AMD GPU resources
(amd.com/gpu) are handled in Kueue quota and admission. Today GPU quota
handling covers NVIDIA resources; AMD Instinct nodes expose amd.com/gpu, and
jobs requesting them must be admitted with correct quota accounting and gang
semantics (all-or-nothing admission via waitForPodsReady).

## Scope

- Define/configure the Kueue resource flavor and ClusterQueue/LocalQueue
  quota model for amd.com/gpu resources on AMD Instinct node pools.
- Ensure admission of multi-pod distributed jobs requesting amd.com/gpu
  preserves gang semantics (no partial admission of a job's pods).
- Validate quota accounting and queueing behavior for jobs requesting
  amd.com/gpu on physical AMD Instinct hardware (hardware access is a shared
  precondition with the serving validation campaign).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a ClusterQueue with an amd.com/gpu flavor, when a workload requests
  amd.com/gpu resources, then quota is accounted against the flavor and
  admission respects the configured quota, measured by Kueue workload
  admission state and quota usage.
- Given a distributed multi-pod workload requesting amd.com/gpu, when the
  full request cannot be met, then the workload remains pending without
  partial pod admission (gang semantics), measured by Kueue admission
  behavior and pending-workload metrics.
- Given queues configured for AMD GPU pools, when training workloads are
  submitted, then they queue and are admitted in order with correct quota
  handling, measured by Kueue pending/admitted workload metrics.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling.

## Risks

- Requires physical AMD Instinct hardware for end-to-end validation; access
  is unresolved at strategy level (procurement or partner lab).
